subject: SymphonyHealth kickoff: streaming + tool-calls schema & runtime plan
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@symphonyhealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@symphonyhealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: SymphonyHealth kickoff: streaming + tool-calls feature enablement

Hi Aisha / Camila,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re excited to move from pilot to production for two capabilities we discussed: low-latency streaming outputs for our triage flow, and the function/tool-calling surface to call our internal lookup API with structured JSON responses.

High-level asks:
- Streaming end-to-end by Jan 20 (alerts and partial results within 300ms p50)
- Tool-call contract: Redwood should call our /patientLookup endpoint and receive back structured JSON (schema attached).
- Schema validation and example payloads for both streaming partials and final JSON outputs.

I attached a short kickoff agenda and the procurement contact is on cc to flag any compliance/contract timing constraints. Can your CS team send a proposed sprint plan and owners for runtime testing, schema sign-off, and go/no-go?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Clinical Integrations | SymphonyHealth

Attachment: 20251202-symphony-kickoff-agenda.pdf (pdf)
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@symphonyhealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SymphonyHealth kickoff: streaming + tool-calls feature enablement

Elena — thank you, and great to meet you over email.

High-level plan (summary):
1) Sprint 0 (this week): finalize JSON schema + example payloads (owner: Monica). Deliverable: schema v1 + unit examples by 2025-12-05.
2) Sprint 1 (12/08–12/19): runtime integration & test harness with streaming enabled; Jonas will lead runtime load tests and latency profiling.
3) Sprint 2 (12/22–01/10): staged canary + partner validation; final go/no-go target 2026-01-20.

Action owners assigned below. I uploaded a working checklist to the shared Drive (link below). I’m also attaching our streaming checklist for internal traceability.

Action owners:
- Monica Patel: schema authoring + schema validation harness (deliver schema v1).
- Jonas Weber: runtime test harness, perf targets, and KV cache sizing recommendations.
- Camila Reyes: CS handoff & integration testing orchestration (customer-facing coordination).
- Me (Aisha): program lead, weekly syncs, exec updates.

Deliverables and milestones are in the Drive folder and I’ll schedule a standing 30-min sync starting 12/08.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20251203-redwood-streaming-checklist.xlsx
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBzSymphonyOnboard
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@symphonyhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Dec 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SymphonyHealth kickoff: streaming + tool-calls feature enablement

Folks — copying the specific asks from the partner into discrete tasks so we can track:
- Monica: please capture both the streaming partials schema (for incremental tokens/events) and the final patient JSON payload. Include `examples/invalid` for common malformed cases.
- Jonas: we need a perf matrix: p50/p90/p99 latency for 1/10/100 concurrent sessions and a recommended batch size. Add a note on how prefix/KV cache will affect interactive latency.
- Aisha: please confirm the on-call expectation during canary and the rollback criteria we’ll present to Symphony.

Also, Monica — I started a schema draft and left inline comments in the JSON. See attachment.

Camila
Camila Reyes | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20251204-json-schema-draft-v1.json
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@symphonyhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2025 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SymphonyHealth kickoff: streaming + tool-calls feature enablement

Thanks — pushed schema v1 to the Drive at the link Aisha shared. Highlights:
- Streaming partial events use `delta` objects with `cursor` and `sequence` to allow idempotent assembly on Symphony side.
- Final `patientRecord` uses typed fields (strings, ISO dates, optional nested arrays) and strict enum values for `status` to avoid downstream parsing errors.
- Added an `errors` envelope to surface validation failures for tool calls.

Questions for Symphony (Elena):
1) Do you want strict schema enforcement (400 on invalid) or lenient (accept + `errors` field) during canary?
2) Any existing JSON Schema validator you prefer on your side (we currently run ajv in the test harness)?

I’ll start the schema validation unit tests once I hear back.

—Monica
Monica Patel | Staff Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@symphonyhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, procurement@symphonyhealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2025 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SymphonyHealth kickoff: streaming + tool-calls feature enablement

Monica — thanks for the v1. For canary we prefer lenient acceptance with `errors` envelope (so we can log and backfill without breaking the pipeline). We will run ajv on our side; I’ll share our validator config by EOD.

Timing check: we’re good to start Sprint 1 on 12/08. Procurement has a short PO process and will aim to clear by 12/12. If you need contract-level confirmation earlier, let me know.

Elena

Attachment referenced: none
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@symphonyhealth.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2025 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SymphonyHealth kickoff: streaming + tool-calls feature enablement

Elena — thanks, noted on lenient mode. Quick runtime notes:
- I’ll provision a 2-node test pool and run an initial latency sweep today. Expected baseline: p50 ~ 180ms, p90 ~ 370ms for our dev weights; I’ll post the concrete numbers + KV cache recommendation in JIRA-RED-1192.
- Rollback criteria: if p50 degrades >25% from baseline or error rate >1% for tool-calls, we auto-fail the canary and revert to the prior model variant.

I’ll add the artifacts to the Drive folder and ping when the harness is live.

Jonas
Jonas Weber | Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference

Related link: JIRA-RED-1192
